name: uninterrupted-work-cycle-designer
description: Design an uninterrupted work cycle with choice-based activities structured within a realistic time block. Use when planning Montessori-style independent work periods or extended choice time.
evidence_sources: Lillard (2005) — Montessori: The Science Behind the Genius
Rosenshine (2012) — Principles of instruction: research-based strategies that all teachers should know (time-on-task)
Csikszentmihalyi (1990) — Flow: the psychology of optimal experience
Diamond & Lee (2011) — Interventions shown to aid executive function development in children 4-12 years old

required.description: The actual time block available — the realistic length of uninterrupted time the timetable allows
The range of activities students can choose from during the work cycle — what is available on the shelves, at the stations, or in the environment

optional.description: How many students in the room
How the classroom currently operates — how often transitions happen, how long students typically work before switching tasks
What the teacher is worried about — off-task behaviour, some students not choosing challenging work, accountability concerns
How the room is organised — whether materials are accessible, whether work areas are defined

fields.description: The complete work cycle structure — opening, work period, and closing, with the teacher's role at each phase
How materials are organised, rotated, and refreshed — what is available and how students choose
What the teacher does during the work cycle — how to observe, when to intervene, and how to record observations
How students enter and exit the work cycle — the routines that support smooth transitions
